title: wrapping the ambient Number or String callee in parentheses does not change which function is called, so the object's coercion member is charged either way
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Inference': 'Requirement inference MUST be transitive through ordinary calls.' `Number(x)` runs `x`'s number-hint coercion and `String(x)` runs its string-hint one, so both are calls whose callee's row must reach the caller. A parenthesis is not an expression: `(Number)(x)` and `Number(x)` call the same function. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS AND WHY IT IS FOUR SPELLINGS: the parenthesised pair was recorded as NOT landable by one lane and landable by a later one, because the two backends had disagreed at exactly this spelling and then converged. It is the kind of divergence that survives a long time, because the rule that recognizes the ambient callee is written against an identifier and a parenthesis is the cheapest thing in the language to forget. The two UNPARENTHESISED spellings are declared alongside on purpose: without them, a backend that had simply started charging every call in this file would satisfy the expectation, and the case would be attributing the refusal to `Number` and `String` on faith. With them, the case says the parenthesised and direct spellings answer identically, which is a statement neither an over-firing nor an under-firing implementation can produce. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: `(JSON).stringify(obj)`, which is a measured shared fail-open on BOTH backends whose cause is the member-receiver helper rather than the ambient-callee rule — it belongs to whoever fixes that helper, and pinning it here would need an `xfail` on both sides. It also does not pin `Math.*`, which is a different table entry, nor the diagnostics' order. `messageContains` is declared once and holds all four to Db, because four refusals at four positions are satisfied by code and position alone whatever the row named; it is the bare capability name because the backends render the row differently (`Db` versus `{Db}`). VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the first declared column from 3 to 5 turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 3c5ad064fc230b2648cb244aa0cc83392257d5060a08e5058956d0027b34877d before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The paired negative control is `coercion-members-that-never-run-charge-nothing`, whose third and fourth positions are a LOCAL binding spelled `Number` and `String` called through the SAME parentheses, which must keep compiling AND RUNNING: the rule has to key on the ambient binding and not on the spelling, and a fix that charges anything called `(Number)(…)` turns that case red rather than passing this one for the wrong reason.
